agent_notes: Ibn Ezra reads רב as 'for a long time' (temporal); most modern versions read it as 'greatly/much'. I kept 'much' in the literal layer, which can carry both, and noted the time reading in the commentary. BBE ('all men are looking down on us') paraphrases away the 'surfeit' image.

Ketiv/Qere in לִגְאֵי יוֹנִים: written as one word לגאיונים, read as two. I glossed the reading (לִגְאֵי יוֹנִים) as 'to the arrogant of oppressors' in the word table and gave the Ketiv in a note. Rashi (on 123:4) records this directly. Ibn Ezra and Radak take the Ketiv as one word like עליונים, from גאה 'be proud'; Metzudat Zion derives it from גאוה plus אונאה; Rashi reads גיא היונים (the valley of the yonim, i.e. Jerusalem) for the phrase, which I regard as homiletic and did not use for the translation. Radak and Meiri explain the construction הלעג השאננים as a construct with the first noun's head elided ('the mockery [of] the at-ease'), and that is how I read it. I left the phrase לִגְאֵי יוֹנִים as 'to the arrogant ones, the oppressors', which is a judgment call; the Hebrew is difficult and 'to the proud oppressors' is a common reading (cf. YLT/ASV 'the proud').
